hypotheses.notes: Differential probe of 8 scenarios (analyzer run on base vs head). One previously-reported diagnostic is now dropped: S4, a closed generic CLASS from a referenced assembly with an unkeyed member. Base reported MsgPack004 twice with Location.None; head reports nothing. All other 7 scenarios identical (no diagnostics on both). Source-declared types: no diagnostic lost in the probe (S1 etc. had none on either side, so this is absence of evidence, not proof). The agent's own UnkeyedMember test (and X-Ray group g1) encode this drop as intended. So: behaviour change confirmed, consistent with the README's stated intent, but broader than the crash fix needed (crash fix is hunk h5; reverting the filter h3 leaves both crash tests green).

Not executable as a test here: whether the defining assembly reports the dropped diagnostics depends on that assembly having been built with the analyzer. Probe S4 shows the consumer-side MsgPack004 existed before and is now gone, so for a library built without the analyzer nobody reports it. Left as a refusal for the owner (R2/R6).

Rejected by reading + running: the shared helper runs the generator on the usage compilation, asserts no Warning-or-higher diagnostics, and Assert.Contains(expectedResolverHintName, hintNames) (e.g. 'App.AppResolver.g.cs'). So the tests do assert a resolver is emitted; REQ-2283-F2 is covered. (All 3 pass on head: runs/2283/timemachine/head.log.)
